q1: How much tennis have you played?
q1a: None yet, or only a handful of times.
q1b: Less than a year, or only now and then.
q1c: 1 to 2 years, about once a week or more.
q1d: More than 2 years of regular play, now or in the past.
q2: Have you played padel, squash, badminton or another racket sport?
q2b: Yes, casually or a long time ago.
q2d: Yes, competitively — club team, leagues or tournaments.
q3: Rallying from the baseline — which is closest to you?
q3a: I'm still learning to get the ball over the net; rallies rarely last more than a couple of shots.
q3b: I can keep a slow rally going with someone at my level, but faster balls or my backhand cause errors.
q3c: I'm consistent at medium pace on both sides, but I can't yet choose direction or depth reliably.
q3d: I can aim medium-paced balls crosscourt or down the line on both sides; depth and spin are still developing.
q4: Serving — which is closest to you?
q4a: I'm still learning the serve; most of my serves don't go in.
q4b: I get serves in with a slow or simplified motion; double faults are common.
q4c: I use a full motion and land most first serves at medium pace; my second serve is just a safe push.
q4d: My second serve is reliable and has some spin, and I can aim my first serve at my opponent's weaker side.
q5: At the net, what can you do reliably?
q5a: I rarely go to the net, or I miss most volleys.
q5b: I can block a volley that comes straight at me; backhand volleys and lobs over my head are a problem.
q5c: Solid volleys on both sides at medium pace; in doubles I'm comfortable playing at the net.
q5d: I come in behind an approach shot, place my volleys with intent, and put away easy overheads.
q6: Which matches do you usually play, and how do they go?
q6a: Mostly lessons or casual hitting — I rarely play scored sets.
q6b: Friendly matches with beginners and improvers.
q6c: Regular competitive matches against intermediate club players; I win about half.
q6d: Club leagues, team matches or tournaments; I usually beat intermediate club players.
